chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Awwad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding a mukatab who enters into a manumission contract, then pays part of his contract and dies, leaving a son and leaving wealth greater than what remains due of the contract, he عليه السلام said: His masters are to be paid what remains of his contract, and whatever remains thereafter belongs to his child.

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: A slave under a contractual arrangement to purchase his freedom
key_terms.لِوَلَدِهِ: For his child, meaning the remaining estate goes to his offspring
key_terms.مَوَالِيهِ: His masters who are entitled to the remaining contract payment
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: His manumission contract and its owed payment

ai.seo_question: If a mukatab dies before finishing his contract, how is his wealth divided?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the estate of a mukatab who dies before completing his manumission payment. The remaining amount of the mukatabah is first paid to his masters, and the rest of the wealth passes to his son as inheritance.
